News.title: Britain’s economy will continue to drift deeper into trouble if Labour refuses to fix their anti-business mindset
News.content:
No firm footing

IN case you didn’t already realise it, the war in Iran is going to cost you. Dearly.

So say the Chancellor and economists.



Well, thanks for the heads-up but what next?



The £480 blow that the Resolution Foundation says each household will suffer this year because of conflict in the Middle East makes the Government’s plan to raise fuel duty from September look even more indefensible.

And Ed Miliband’s ruinously expensive Net Zero fantasies, crippling families and businesses with sky-high energy costs while endangering Britain’s fuel security, look totally perverse.

But energy costs are not the only thing holding back British industry.

It seems utterly crazy that our manufacturers are losing business because of skill shortages when we have nearly one million 16-24 year-olds dumped on the jobs scrapheap, not helped by the Government’s policies making them too expensive to hire.

Entrepreneur Jo Bamford’s suggestion to link school pupils with factory chiefs — to guide them towards the blue-collar industries that need them ­— makes perfect sense.

It would help the youngsters, the local communities they live in and the hard-working taxpayers forced to foot a ballooning benefits bill.

The other major skill shortage Mr Bamford rightly highlights is the lack of business-minded leaders in the Government.

Until that changes, Britain’s economic growth will continue to falter, war or no war.



Hell for hols

IT’S no use thinking that you can escape the economic misery with a well-earned staycation.

For those who can’t afford a foreign getaway (if jet fuel shortages don’t scupper those as well), Labour’s fun police are determined to put the squeeze on holidays in the UK too.

They will cost an extra £500 million a year if the Government goes ahead with a planned “tourist tax”, the Confederation of British Industry warns.

The new levy on overnight stays would not only seriously stretch the budgets of hard-pushed British families seeking a break in this country but cripple investment and growth for a hospitality sector already struggling since the pandemic and hit by devastating business rate hikes.

The Government — supposedly laser focused on economic growth and helping with the cost of living — seems remarkably determined to make both much worse.



Up for the Cup

THERE is some good news at least.

The Government has confirmed that Britain’s pubs and bars will be able to stay open late for every World Cup match featuring England or Scotland that kicks off before 10pm this summer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That makes it more important than ever that both sides don’t go out at the group stages.

We’ll drink to that!

News.title: Sobbing dad of teen girl savaged to death by dog describes horror in house as ‘loving’ family Lurcher attacked them
News.content:
THE father of a teenager killed by her pet lurcher told The Sun the attack was “completely out of the blue”.

Jack Biscoe found 19-year-old Jamie-Lea at home with a bite wound to her neck from female Shy.





Emergency services were called to the property in Leaden Roding, Essex, at 10.45pm but she was pronounced dead at the scene.

Last night, Jack, 37, told The Sun that the blue-merle lurcher, which has been seized by cops, as the “softest dog”.

He said the dog had no history of biting or ­aggressive behaviour — adding: “My daughter was not killed by an XL Bully, she was killed by a genuine family dog.”

Horse trainer Jack described the seven-year–old pet, which he bought as a puppy at seven weeks, as Jamie-Lea’s “best friend” and said she even slept on his daughter’s bed.



He is now warning other families “just how quick a dog can take away a life”.

He said: “Witnessing the horror and destruction it has caused me, it’s not worth it. Treat them as dogs, give them their beds, be careful.”

Jack also urged other pet owners that dangerous dogs are not “breed specific”.

He added: “I thought I could trust that dog with my life and it took my daughter’s life.”



The dad of one, who raised Jamie-Lea alone, discovered her unconscious in his bedroom after coming home from KFC with his partner Steven Daniels, 43, on Friday night.

She was collapsed on the floor between his bed and bedside table.

As Jack tried to save her life with CPR, lurcher Shy began to attack him too.



She bit off part of his ear, which will require reconstructive surgery, and left puncture wounds in his arms.

His other two dogs Bella and Mouse — Shy’s 18-month-old pups — were downstairs at the time.

Police seized all three animals and Jack was arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury resulting in death.

He was released on bail on ­Saturday night.

Last night, he paid tribute to his daughter, who recently finished studying childcare at college. He said: “She was my best friend.”



He described her death as “so painful”, adding: “I don’t know how to step forward without that child in my life. She was my only child.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Colin Spender, from the Canine and Feline Behaviour Association, said: “It’s very unusual for a lurcher to cause fatal injuries. It’s unheard of.”

But the expert, who has been training dogs for over 30 years, added: “Any dog is capable of causing serious injuries.”

News.title: No Glasto, no Wireless but still plenty of festival action this year – our ultimate guide to the best outdoor concerts
News.content:
IF there is one thing the UK does well, it is ­festivals. So brace yourself, because the 2026 season promises to be a big one.

Glastonbury may be taking a well-earned break to let the land at ­Worthy Farm recover, while Wireless was cancelled after headliner Kanye West was blocked from entering the UK over his Nazi-style rants.



But there are still tons of fantastic events around the country where you can get your groove on.

Whether you love headbanging, skanking to militant basslines or belting out the biggest pop hits, there is something for everyone.

Here, we round up the biggest and best.



There are lots more we couldn’t squeeze in, so check what is happening in your local area.

Tickets are usually available for days and weekends.

Prices can vary, so go to individual websites.

In the meantime, grab some beers, dig out that tent and don’t forget your wellies as Tom Bryden gives you the lowdown on the summer’s hottest fests.

BEST FOR TEENS



BOARDMASTERS (August 5-9): Set across Watergate Bay and Fistral Beach – two Newquay sites ­overlooking the Cornish coast – this music and surfing festival might have the most beautiful setting of any of those listed here.

On offer is a broad range of artists, both old and new, including Lily Allen, Kasabian, Joy Crookes and Alessi Rose, plus dance offerings from Fatboy Slim, Goldie, Girls Don’t Sync, Bushbaby and more.



READING & LEEDS (August 27-30): It is the definitive post-GCSE summer sesh – and it is going to be a big one.

Charli XCX, Dave, Fontaines D.C., Raye, Sombr, Geese, Gunna . . . in fact, just about everything that under-30s are listening to is on the line-up.

This lot are just the tip of the iceberg.

PARKLIFE (June 20-21): This popular festival returns to Manchester’s Heaton Park for two days of tunes.

Soundtracks from DJs including Calvin Harris, Sammy Virji and Chris Stussy, grime legend Skepta and ­Swedish pop queen Zara Larsson will keep fans on their toes.



There is a real dance focus this year, so have your shades at the ready.

BEST FOR THE DISCERNING MUSO

END OF THE ROAD (September 3-6): Taking over Larmer Tree Gardens on the Dorset/Wiltshire border, this small, independent festival has built a reputation for combining eclectic acts and critically acclaimed artists, leaving no genre untouched.

Helping to celebrate its 20th anniversary this year are Pulp, Canadian lo-fi indie pioneer Mac DeMarco, Irish singer-songwriter CMAT, plus a host of other acts that will make you feel like a Mercury Prize judge.

GOTTWOOD (June 11-14): Hidden in the woodlands of the Carreglwyd Estate, this magical little electronic-focused festival is celebrating its 15th anniversary.

For the first time, it has a 24-hour licence, so get ready to party non-stop on the Isle of Anglesey, off the coast of Wales, to the best in genre-bending dance.



Enjoy serious drum and bass from the likes of ­Mantra and Samurai Breaks, housey numbers from Octo Octa or the hypnotising ambient techno of Priori.

BEST FOR HEAD- BANGERS

DOWNLOAD (June 10-14): The UK’s largest rock festival returns to Donington Park in Leicestershire this summer.

Nu-metal acts Linkin Park and Limp Bizkit will headline alongside Guns N’ Roses, stoking some serious mosh pit carnage.

Sold out but resale tickets are available.

ARCTANGENT (August 19-22): This festival at Fernhill Farm near Bristol has established itself as a mecca for lovers of experimental and cutting-edge sounds – from post-rock to math-rock, prog and everything in between.



Check out the mind-melting melodies of ­Cardiacs, the irreverent weirdness of Primus and the brilliant horror of French blackgazers Alcest.

BEST FOR FAMILIES

LATITUDE (July 23-26): There will be the traditional pink sheep galore – and so much more – at the 20th anniversary bonanza of music, arts, comedy and fun at Henham Park, near Southwold in Suffolk.

You will be able to enjoy acts including Lewis Capaldi, David Byrne, Teddy Swims and Billy Ocean, as well as a bunch of up-and-comers.



Plus comedians including Jack Dee, Sue Perkins and Lenny Henry are ready to have you doubled over with laughter. And don’t miss the talks from scientists, either.

CAMP BESTIVAL (July 30-August 2): Alongside headliners Self Esteem, Bastille and Fatboy Slim, this kids’ paradise at Lulworth Castle, near ­Dorset’s Jurassic Coast, champions family wellbeing – with beekeeping workshops, skateboarding and trampolining.

Beyond the headliners are a host of artists, DJs and even some musical Tibetan monks.

BEST ALL-ROUNDER

ISLE OF WIGHT (June 18-21): Head to Newport’s Seaclose Park, off the south coast, for one of the country’s most legendary festivals and enjoy something different every day.

Fans will be treated to Lewis Capaldi’s ­tearjerkers and Calvin Harris’s dancefloor anthems, rounded off by none other than The Cure.



And that’s just the main stage…

BEST FOR PEOPLE WHO HATE CAMPING

TRNSMT (June 19-21): Glasgow Green is ready to go music-mad this summer as TRNSMT returns to the city centre.

Alongside hometown hero Lewis Capaldi, there will be sets from Nineties legend Richard Ashcroft, disco king Nile Rodgers and plenty more.

THE GREAT ESCAPE(May 13-16): Brighton is hardly lacking when it comes to music, but for four days next month, more than 450 up-and-coming artists will take over just about every pub, club and venue to show what they are made of.



Before his rise to stardom, Ed Sheeran ­performed at the festival in 2011, while the 1975 were there in 2013.

All venues are within walking distance of each other – and you might get to see the next big thing.

GALA (May 22-24): Peckham Rye Park in South ­London is the place to be on May bank holiday ­weekend, with a huge, three-day line-up of rap, bass and dance, including a homecoming set from Giggs, plus magic behind the decks fromf ­Conducta, DJ Seinfeld and Todd Terje.

BEST FOR PEOPLE STUCK IN THE 80s

REWIND (August 21-23): There is no holding back the nostalgia at this Oxfordshire festival dedicated to the Eighties.

Headlining at Temple Island Meadows in Henley-on-Thames, are The Human League and The Proclaimers, but there will also be sets from Kim Wilde, Soul II Soul, Blancmange, Toyah and Peter Andre.

News.title: I’ve met school shooters but ‘I Don’t Like Mondays’ killer Brenda Spencer is different… she’s an icon to evil
News.content:
AS nine-year-old Monica Selvig walked into her primary school, on an ordinary Monday morning in January, she felt a sharp pain in her side and fell to the floor, unaware she had been shot.

Moments later, eight-year-old Mary Clark was hit by a second bullet, in her stomach, which sent a red stain spreading across her white top.



Within minutes, eight children at the Grover Cleveland primary school in San Diego had been hit by an unseen sniper in a tragic chain of events that would leave two brave staff members dead.

The horrific murders in 1979, carried out by 16-year-old Brenda Spencer, provided a blueprint for subsequent ‘school shooter’ incidents in the US.



School shooting incidents have soared since, with 1,300 incidents since the 1970s, and 185 deaths since Columbine, in 1999.

When asked why she targeted kids in the seemingly motiveless shooting, from the bedroom window of her house across the street from the school, Spencer replied: “I just don’t like Mondays” – a callous response which inspired the Boomtown Rats song I Don’t Like Mondays later that same year.

Almost five decades on Spencer, who was recently refused bail, remains a notorious character in the American psyche.

“I speak to about 12 school shooters and I’ve met quite a few of them and Brenda is just this enigma. She’s different from the rest,” says journalist N Leigh Hunt, who has spent a decade researching the case for the book, I Don’t Like Mondays, and has spoken to Spencer.

“She’s female, which at the time I started writing was odd, although there have been others since.



“Whether we like it or not, Brenda is an American icon. She is actually in every part of American society. Any woman who wears aviator glasses and a skullcap walks into down the street, people are in fear because that was Brenda Spencer. We already had female criminals, like the Manson sisters and Patty Hearst. But Brenda was another level. And she had no idea what she was doing.”

Troubled teen Brenda Spencer was a painfully thin, 5ft 2in tomboy who lived with her father Wally and older brother Scott in the modest, unkempt house across from the school.

Her mother, Dorothy, had left Wally in a row over his cheating, in 1972, and Brenda felt “neglected” by her mum.

I just started shooting. I just did it for the fun of it. I just don’t like Mondays. I did this because it’s a way to cheer up the day. Brenda Spencer,16-year-old shooter

She would later claim she was sexually abused by her father, who also beat her regularly, because she reminded him of her mother.

“I was neglected by my mother and father,” she said in a statement after her arrest. “My mother by being emotionally distant, and my father in my day-to-day care. I was pretty much left to fend for myself. I had to cook my own meals every day from the age of eight.”



She added: “When I was nine years old, my father started touching me and fondling me. I had to sleep in the same bed with him, and almost every night he would do something.”

She claimed she was bullied at school, for being unwashed, and was verbally abused by her older siblings, Tess and Scott.

She began using drugs and alcohol at around the age of 12 and suffered from bouts of depression.

Introduced to hunting at a young age, Brenda had a fascination with weapons and boasted to her friends that she wanted to kill a police officer by “blowing his head off.”

For Christmas, in 1978, dad Wally thought she deserved a reward for her hard work at school and bought her a 10/22 Ruger semi-automatic rifle and 500 rounds of ammo.



The gun, advertised as the perfect starter weapon for the inexperienced, was more than half her height, weighed just 5lbs five pounds and held a 10-round rotary magazine.

Just a month later she told her dad she was too sick to go to school before picking up the Ruger and a pellet gun and, as kids as young as four arrived at the gates opposite, she opened fire.

Honing in on pupils in blue or red coats, she mowed down eight victims, the youngest being just seven.

Brenda, I believe,was trying to give a performance. She was trying to get on the TV. She was trying to be famous. She had a little bit of a little person’s complex. She was showing off to friends. N Leigh Hunt, Journalist

After hearing two shots, the school’s principal, Burton Wragg, rushed outside to bring children to safety – straight into the line of fire.

“Duck, you guys! Crystal, run!” were his last words before he fell to the ground, with two gunshot wounds in his chest. He later died in hospital.



Janitor Mike Suchar ran to help Burton but was himself fatally wounded. All the time, amid the chaos, kids were still being dropped off at the school.

As police raced to the site, a reporter from a local newspaper, the Evening Tribune, thumbed through the address book and called houses facing the school, to garner witness accounts.

Incredibly Brenda, alone in the house, picked up the phone and instantly outed herself as the shooter.

“I just started shooting. That’s it. I just did it for the fun of it,” she told him, calmly. “I just don’t like Mondays. I did this because it’s a way to cheer up the day. Nobody likes Mondays.”

Author Nicholas thinks this “bravado” holds the key to the real motive behind the shooting spree.



“Brenda, I believe,was trying to give a performance,” he says. “She was trying to get on the TV. She was trying to be famous. She had a little bit of a little person’s complex. She was showing off to friends.”

He also feels she may not have meant to kill. “She shot her gun and her BB gun, her little pellet gun, at the same time so she discharged two weapons that day.

“You won’t see that in the news because they don’t want to advertise that because that gives doubt to her motive.

“She’s not going to kill anybody with a pellet gun and she had the lowest calibre gun that could be bought.



“I think when she realised what she’d actually done, she started to panic. She hid in the house for six hours until she eventually came out. Everything after that has been bravado.

“I believe she had no idea what she was doing. She just literally was a dimwitted, immature child looking for attention.”

Finally arrested after a six-hour standoff, Brenda was tried as an adult and, on April 4, 1980, the day after her 19th birthday, she was sentenced to concurrent terms of 25 years in prison.

She remains in custody in the California Institution for Women after several failed bids for parole.



In a parole statement, in 2009, Brenda said: “There are many factors that could have led up to my crime, such as sexual abuse, physical abuse, depression, verbal abuse, neglect, problems in school, drugs, and alcohol.”

Media reports at the time painted her father as an abusive, poverty-stricken alcoholic and claimed he and Brenda slept on a single mattress on the floor in her living room.

But Nicholas says that paints a false picture that feeds into myths about school shooters.

“So many lies surround this – the dad was a drunk and he had no money. Just not true. Yes, dad was a weirdo, a cheapskate. But they had property in Potrero 50 miles down the road in the hills where they used to go shooting their guns.

She had lots of friends but they were known as the weird family. I think she just needed a bit more attention than the average kid. N Leigh Hunt, Journalist

“They make out he was drunk and sleeping in the lounge with his daughter. It’s not true. They didn’t live alone. The brother lived in the house. The sister had just moved out of the house. They had their own bedrooms.



“This family dynamic was not as it was portrayed. We created this belief in America that school shooters are these loner children of divorced parents who kill cats and are psychopaths. They are just children who have major issues that nobody’s watching.

“You go to the Columbine shooting (1999) and both those perpetrators have parents who are together. The vast majority of school shooters have parents that are together. There’s no real commonality with this.”

Wally denied the sexual abuse claims but, in a bizarre twist, went on to have a relationship with Brenda’s former cellmate, getting her pregnant when she was 17 and he was 50, and eventually marrying her.

But Nicholas says, with her history of lies, Brenda’s claims of abuse should be taken with a pinch of salt.

“There was anger between her parents, she wasn’t getting much attention from her mother. and her father was an absent dad,” he says.



“She had lots of friends but they were known as the weird family. I think she just needed a bit more attention than the average kid.

“With regards to the abuse, there’s no doubt that her father was a creep, knocking up her cellmate who was underage, then taking her to Arizona for their shotgun wedding.

“But there was no evidence at the time that he was doing anything horrible to Brenda and the brother and the sister both deny it happened.

“I’m not in a position to say that anybody who speaks about abuse is a liar. But the evidence is really thin.

“Brenda’s done everything she possibly can to make you disbelieve her but then Wally’s done everything he possibly can to make you believe it.



“Every story Brenda has told since the time I met her, there’s slight bits of bravado. Whether it’s fighting in prison, how good she was as a photographer, or how she could grow corn in prison from a microwave popcorn bag.

“There’s an element of bravado and theatre.

“Almost fifty years on her story is becoming more and more elaborate.”

Named by some as “the mother” of school shooters, Brenda has herself professed guilt over copycat killings, saying: “With every school shooting, I feel I’m partially responsible. What if they got the idea from what I did?”

But with casualties increasing, year after year, Nicholas believes we have a lot to learn from the original.



“It’s all about warning signs and triggers.

“Psychologists will often put every school shooter, murderer or children killer into categories, after the fact. But nothing they have concluded, or the FBI has concluded, has done anything to stop the problem.

“All of the behavioural analysis has never stopped one serial killer. Psychology is fantastic but the average folk, you and me, we still have this problem.

“There’s no one case that says this is what school shooters do and that’s why it’s such a scary story.

“Any child in America at any given time could take their parents’ weapon and just go bang, bang on the streets so I think the community – family, friends, neighbours – have to look out for the trigger warnings.”

News.title: Family of woman, 19, who died after attack by ‘pet dog who slept on her bed’ launch fundraiser – as man, 37, arrested
News.content:
PET TRAGEDY Family of woman, 19, who died after attack by ‘pet dog who slept on her bed’ launch fundraiser – as man, 37, arrested

THE family of a “kind and beautiful” 19-year-old girl who died after she was reportedly attacked by her pet have paid tribute to her.

Jamie-Lea Biscoe was killed after her family pet of seven years allegedly attacked her at home in Essex on Saturday.





In a previous tribute on Facebook, Jamie’s grandmother Tina Wells said the lurcher cross had “slept on my granddaughter’s bed”.

Her aunt Maria Biscoe has launched a gofundme to raise money for Jamie’s funeral costs and “give her the best send off”.

Maria wrote: “Jamie was tragically attacked and killed at her home by her pet dog.

“She had been the family pet for 7 years and had never shown any sign of aggression before this sad tragic incident.

“Jamie-Lea was the kindest, most beautiful young adult and would have done anything for anyone.

“She loved life and her family but most of all she adored her dad Jack.

“We are trying to raise funds to pay for her funeral, so we can give her the best send off.



“Thank you for all of your support! RIP Jamie-Lea Bisco.”

So far the fundraiser has raised £2,215 of its £5,000 goal.

Assistant Chief Constable Stuart Hooper from Essex Police said today: “Our thoughts remain with all those who knew and loved Jamie-Lea.

“Her young life has been so tragically cut short.

“Our detectives are continuing to work around the clock to establish exactly what happened and specialist officers are continuing to support Jamie-Lea’s family.



“This is unimaginable for her loved ones and friends and, as such, I would ask people to respect their grief and privacy at this extremely difficult time.”

A 37-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury that led to death.

He has since been released on bail until July while police inquiries continue.

The dog, which was a family pet and believed to be a lurcher cross, was seized and tests are under way to formally establish the exact breed, according to police.

Jamie-Lea was declared dead at the scene after police rushed to her home at 10.45pm on Saturday.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officers remain at the scene and they urge anyone with information to get in touch.

News.title: Teacher, 25, caught having sexual relationships with two teen boys ‘she knew from family friends’
News.content:
TWISTED AFFAIR Teacher, 25, caught having sexual relationships with two teen boys ‘she knew from family friends’

A TEACHER has been caught having sexual relationships with two teenage boys whom she reportedly knew through family friends.

Shelby Dawn Lashombe, 25, pleaded guilty to having sex with both minors – after she was seen kissing one of the 16-year-old students.





A bystander who witnessed her inappropriate behaviour with the pupil alerted cops before they arrested Lashombe.

She reportedly knew both boys were under the age of consent – and had even been family friends with one of them for years before the twisted relationship, according to arrest documents.

Neither of the two young victims were students at Valley Mills High School in Texas where she worked at the time of her arrest last September.

McLennan County Police received a tip-off that the teacher was seen kissing a 16-year-old boy, it was reported.

The teen confirmed he had sexual intercourse with Lashombe.

He also said “it has happened more than once” and that the teacher knew he was underage, according to an affidavit.

Lashombe later told cops she was intimate with the teenage boy – and admitted she had been seeing him for the past six months.

The documents say: “Shelby stated she had been friends with the juvenile’s family for years, knowing his age and that he was a student.”



Lashombe also told police she was having sex with a second boy who was under the age of 17.

The second victim attended a different school to the first victim, the documents reveal.

On Friday, the former teacher was recommended to be placed on deferred probation and fined $1,000 after pleading guilty.

She faced two counts of an improper relationship between an educator and a student.

Both charges are second-degree felonies – and she now faces up to 20 years behind bars.



In exchange for Lashombe’s guilty pleas, two counts of sexual assault against a child were dropped.

These two charges are also second-degree felonies.

Judge Thomas West ordered a presentence investigation by probation officers, which he will consider before deciding to accept the plea bargain.

Lashombe is set to be sentenced on June 26.

News.title: Pigtailed social worker, 29, sexually assaulted schoolboy under 12 & asked him to be her boyfriend
News.content:
SICK MISS Pigtailed social worker, 29, sexually assaulted schoolboy under 12 & asked him to be her boyfriend

A MARRIED school social worker has narrowly avoided jail time after pleading guilty to sexually assaulting an underage student.

Chloe Rose Castro was sentenced to 20 years to life of Sex Offender Intensive Supervision Probation (ISP) after having a sexual relationship with a sixth-grade boy.





The 29-year-old will also serve three years in community corrections before probation.

Appearing in mugshots wearing pigtail, she must also register as a sex offender for life.

The victim will also receive $14,000 in restitution.

Castro was taken into custody after the victim’s parents notified the Arvada Police Department back in October 2024.

They handed over evidence that showed the former social worker engaging in an inappropriate relationship with their child.

The exact age of the boy is unclear but those in sixth grade are typically between 11 and 12 years old.

An affidavit – obtained by 9News – revealed the child’s parents discovered inappropriate Instagram messages between their son and Castro.

It is thought the married woman first met the victim at the end of his sixth-grade year.



According to the document, it wasn’t before long that she asked him to be her boyfriend.

When the boy’s parents tried to take his phone from him, the child quickly logged out of all his accounts and changed his passwords.

However, it wasn’t before the boy’s father saw messages from “Chloe Castro”, as well as multiple exchanges with a “Jeremy”.

During a police interview, the victim confirmed he saved Castro’s number under “Jeremy”, and that they met up while he was still finishing sixth grade.

He also confessed that Castro asked him to be her boyfriend, and even that they planned to move to New Mexico together.



To make matters worse, it was revealed that Castro was married but that she and her husband had an understanding that she could have two partners.

“There is no sentence that I could ask for which will give the community their trust back in Jefferson County Public Schools,” the prosecutor said in court.

“There is not a sentence that will take away the trauma this child suffered.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Castro then addressed the court, saying that she is committed to treatment.

The disgraced educator added that she will never work with children again.

News.title: Paranoid Putin boosting air defences around secret fortress he shares with ‘lover and sons’ out of fear for their safety
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin has yet again boosted air defences around his remote palace where the paranoid dictator hides with his secret “wife” and their two sons.

A fresh ring of steel has been thrown up around the Valdai fortress -the tyrant’s main home during the war – and it’s now better protected than most Russian cities.





The bunker is now encircled by 27 modern air defence system emplacements, according to new research from Radio Liberty.

At least eight new air defence towers have been fitted in four months since Putin falsely claimed Ukraine had attacked the luxury hideaway.

He is believed to reside there with secret alleged lover, Olympic gymnast Alina Kabaeva, 42, and their two sons, Swiss-born Ivan, 11, and Moscow-born Vladimir, six.



A Ukrainian strike at the end of last year targeted other buildings elsewhere in the Novgorod region – but Putin tried to moan to Donald Trump that Kyiv was seeking to hit him and his family.

Western and Ukrainian intelligence reported the Russian dictator’s claims were false – with the US president also disagreeing with Putin’s cries.

But months later, the paranoid Kremlin despot has again tightened his defences following rumours that Kabaeva refused to remain at the palace.

The fortress, 230 miles northwest of Moscow, is believed to be equipped with its own nuclear bunker and hospital.



In 2024, there were only seven air defence placements guarding the Valdai complex – now there are almost four times as many.

Most of the current 27 placements are believed to be Pantsir systems – costing up to £16million each.

But at least one is understood to be an S-400 system, costing as much as £800million.

Sophisticated radar systems also protect the palace and the family he has never revealed to ordinary Russian people.

The overall cost of the equipment guarding this Putin palace is well over £1billion.



The entire city of Moscow with 20 million residents and the surrounding region have just 100 air defence emplacements, according to reports – and other Russian cities have even fewer.

The sprawling Valdai complex among forests and lakes includes a main house and a separate residence for Kabaeva and the children.

In December, Ukraine launched a long-range drone strike on the Akron chemicals plant – key to Russian explosives manufacture – in Veliky Novgorod, 85 miles from Valdai.



In a desperate false claim, the Kremlin said more than 90 Ukrainian drones had been directed at Putin.

His young sons are hidden under the surname Spiridonov, according to top Russian journalists, and educated by tutors outside of normal schools.

The children are keen young gymnasts who have been seen in bombshell footage.

Spiridonov appears to be a family name linked to the first name of Putin’s colourful paternal grandfather Spiridon Putin, who lived from 1879 to 1965, dying on his 86th birthday.

Spiridon was the personal chef for the founder of the Soviet Union, Vladimir Lenin, and also cooked for his widow Nadezhda before preparing meals for tyrant Josef Stalin in the Kremlin.



Earlier, he had served notorious mad monk Rasputin while working at the legendary Hotel Astoria in St Petersburg in the tsarist era.

Ukraine in February claimed to have destroyed half of all Russia’s Pantsir air defence systems.

Putin’s relationship with Kabaeva started after the tyrant broke from another secret mistress Svetlana Krivonogikh, 50, mother of his love child Luiza Rozova, 23.



Proekt said: “Located about the same distance from Putin and Kabaeva’s houses is a huge spa complex with a solarium, a cryo chamber, a 25-metre swimming pool, a hammam, a sauna, a mud room, massage baths, cosmetology and dentistry areas.”

The investigation reveals there is a “constant presence of children in the residence”.

“In the summers of 2020 and 2021, a small karting track was set up on the site of the former helipads.

“And right next to the residence, a large children’s playground in yellow and blue was erected deep in the woods between 2016 and 2020.”

Putin uses his “personal armoured train” to travel to his lakeside hideout.



“For this reason, a secret, guarded station was built near his residence,” Proekt reported.

News.title: Bird flu warning issued in Europe as WHO says 'avoid contact'
News.content:
Bird flu warning issued in Europe as WHO says 'avoid contact'

The World Health Organization has issued guidance after a man was diagnosed with H9N2 bird flu in Italy - the first time this strain has been imported into Europe

View 2 Images The case marks the first time this particular strain has been imported into Europe (Image: Getty Images)

Health authorities are on high alert following a man being diagnosed with a high-risk strain of bird flu in Italy. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has confirmed this marks the first occasion the A(H9N2) subtype has been imported into Europe, triggering concerns about a potential fresh health crisis.

‌



The patient, an adult male, had recently returned from a six-month period in Senegal before arriving in Italy. He was taken to an emergency department experiencing a fever and a persistent cough.

‌



While the WHO currently assesses the risk to the general population as "low," they have cautioned that any human infection caused by a novel influenza A virus has the "potential for high public health impact."

‌



In a warning to the public, the WHO has urged people to steer clear of dangerous environments to stop the spread of the bug.

The global health body said: "The public should avoid contact with high-risk environments such as live animal markets/farms or surfaces that might be contaminated by poultry faeces.", reports the Daily Star.

"Respiratory protection is highly recommended for those handling live or dead (including slaughtering) poultry in occupational or backyard-farming settings. Good hand hygiene, i.e. frequent washing of hands or the use of alcohol-based hand sanitiser is recommended." Experts have cautioned that the bird flu strain can trigger a variety of symptoms in humans. While some may only experience mild respiratory problems, the WHO warned it can result in severe illness and death, conjunctivitis, gastrointestinal pain and encephalitis (brain swelling).

‌



View 2 Images WHO has issued guidance in the wake of the infection (Image: CDC and NIAID/AFP via Getty Imag)

In the most recent case, the patient faced a double blow, as tests additionally revealed he was battling tuberculosis. He was swiftly placed in a "negative-pressure isolation room" as medical staff raced to contain the virus.

The situation grew more puzzling when the patient informed investigators he had "no known history of exposure to poultry" or any infected individuals prior to falling ill.

‌



Early genetic analysis suggests the infection was most likely contracted from an "avian source" in Senegal, where the virus is known to circulate amongst bird populations.

Despite the man's stable condition, the WHO is leaving nothing to chance. They said: "According to the International Health Regulations, a human infection caused by a novel influenza A virus subtype is an event that has the potential for high public health impact and must be notified to the WHO."

Close contacts of the man in both Italy and Senegal have been traced and placed under surveillance, with some even receiving preventive antiviral medication to halt a full-scale outbreak before it takes hold.

Article continues below

While the WHO maintains that the likelihood of the virus spreading between humans remains "low," they are "continuing to monitor these viruses and the situation globally" as the threat continues to loom over Europe.

News.title: '100 easyJet passengers' miss flight in Milan after border control delays
News.content:
'100 easyJet passengers' miss flight in Milan after border control delays

British passengers have been left stranded at Linate airport in Milan due to huge delays at border control have meant they missed their flight back to Manchester

View 3 Images Passengers were left stranded (Image: X/Emily_Benn20)

More than 100 easyJet passengers are allegedly stranded in Milan after their flight left without them.

‌



Many people have taken to social media to complain that they faced long queues of up to three hours at border control as they sought to fly out from the Italian city’s Linate airport.

‌



And there are reports that some passengers had become ill after waiting in the heat for their easyJet flight on Sunday night back to Manchester Airport.

‌



UK to sizzle at 22C within days as heatwave hits 6 counties READ MORE :

Keir Starmer sends warning to US and Iran after peace talks break down READ MORE :

Speaking with the Echo, Vicky Chapman, 26, from Pensby in Wirral, had been due to fly back to Manchester on Monday morning with her five-year-old son Fredrik and family after a holiday. She said she was among 105 passengers left stranded at Milan Linate Airport when their 11am flight departed without them.

View 3 Images Vicky Chapman from the Wirral with partner Adam Hoijord, son Fredrik, mother Lynne Chapman and brother Dan Chapman.

The flight was reportedly held for 59 minutes as passengers were delayed at passport control, but eventually took off as the crew approached the end of their permitted working hours.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Vicky, her partner Adam Hoijord, son Fredrik, mother Lynne Chapman and brother Dan Chapman are now unable to leave Milan until Tuesday.

She said: “We got to the airport with more than enough time and reached our gate at 9.30am, but we were refused entry through passport control. We were then told we were a ‘no show’ for the flight because we didn’t reach the gate on time, even though there were issues at passport control and they wouldn’t let us through.

‌



“We were passed from pillar to post for three hours and no-one helped us. It was so hot in the airport, people were vomiting and close to passing out. We’re now being told Tuesday is the earliest we can get back, and that we’ll have to fly to Gatwick. We’ve also had to pay for an Airbnb out of our own pocket.”

View 3 Images EasyJet passenger said they have been left stranded in Milan (stock image) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Easyjet reportedly said it was supporting passengers but that the situation was not in their control.

‌



Kiera, 17, from Oldham, says she and her boyfriend now face a 20-hour wait at the airport until they could get another flight tomorrow. "We got here at 7.30pm for our flight at 11pm so were super early. We got to Border Control and it was a massive queue of people. I wasn't feeling great anyway because I think I'd got food poisoning," Kiera told the BBC.

"At about 10.50pm they brought some water over for people, and when we got to the front of the queue someone asked us if we were going to Manchester, and told us our flight had just gone. There were only about 30 people got on the plane, and about 100 people didn't." Kiera said that it will now cost £520 for new flights and they will have to travel to Gatwick rather than Manchester.

Easyjet has blamed delays at passport control over the new new European Entry/Exit System brought in last October. A spokeswoman said: "We are aware that some passengers departing from Milan Linate today experienced longer than usual waiting times at passport control and we advised customers due to fly to allow additional time to make their way through the airport.

Article continues below

"We have been doing all possible to minimise the impact of the airport queues, holding flights to allow customers extra time and providing free flight transfers for any customers who may have missed their flight including EJU5420 to Manchester.

"We continue to urge border authorities to ensure they make full and effective use of the permitted flexibilities for as long as needed while European Entry / Exit System is implemented, to avoid these unacceptable border delays for our customers. While this is outside of our control, we are sorry for any inconvenience caused."

News.title: Trump's naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz - what it means for the world
News.content:
Trump's naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz - what it means for the world

The continued escalation between Iran and the US in the Strait of Hormuz - which typically sees a fifth of the world's oil pass though it - could lead to another hit in the 'cost of living' and more economic chaos, experts warn

View 5 Images Donald Trump warned vessels attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump warned that the US Navy would start a blockade of the all-important Strait of Hormuz after peace talks with Iran fell apart, marking a new low in the Middle East war.

‌



The US President in a fiery message online said the Navy would stop any vessel that has paid Iran a huge toll to leave or entre the waterway. This comes after Tehran effectively closed off the Strait of Hormuz, which sees one fifth of the world's oil supply pass through it on a regular day, after the US and Israel started bombing Iran on February 28.

‌



Washington and Tehran agreed on a fragile two-week ceasefire earlier this week but the pause in fighting broke down as Israel continued to attack Iran-aligned Hezbollah, in Lebanon. The Trump blockade of the Strait could help plunge to global economy into further chaos.

‌



View 5 Images Oil tankers and cargo ships lining up in the Strait of Hormuz, on Wednesday (Image: AP)

Donald Trump health fears resurface as he 'limps' down stairs of Air Force One READ MORE :

Vice President JD Vance flew to Islamabad, Pakistan, for peace talks with Iran but said negotiators from Iran "have chosen not to accept our terms" and added that he will "go back to the United States, having not come to an agreement".

Iran hit back and said the US "ultimately failed to gain the trust of the Iranian delegation" during peace talks. Trump quickly followed with his raging rant and threat to vessels attempting to cross the crucial waterway between Iran and Oman.

‌



View 5 Images JD Vance smiles despite failing to negotiate a peace deal with Iran (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

In a dramatic Truth Social post, the Commander-in-Chief said the talks fell apart to a disagreement on Iran owning nuclear weapons and wrote: "I have instructed our navy to seek and interdict every vessel in international waters that has paid a toll to Iran. No one who pays and illegal toll will have safe passage on the high seas. We will also begin destroying mines the Iranians laid in the Straits. Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!"

The global economy has already been rocked by the chaos in the Strait of Hormuz, with oil prices soaring from around $70 a barrel before the conflict started to shooting up to around $120 at its worst during the conflict.

‌



View 5 Images Vessels stuck around the Strait of Hormuz

The ceasefire announcement and hope shipping could start to continue normally saw the price of a barrel fall to $92 after the fragile deal was announced. The previous rising price of oil indirectly led to a hike in prices at the pumps. The RAC revealed that a tank of petrol is now £13.86 more expensive than it was at the beginning of the Middle East conflict at £86.92.

Mohamed El-Erian, an adviser to insurer Allianz and an ex-president of Queens’ College, University of Cambridge, told The Guardian how the uncertainty caused by the continued war and blockades could hit the UK.

‌



He said: "Absent a swift resumption of negotiations, the immediate reaction of financial markets when they open for the trading week will be to push oil prices higher and borrowing costs higher." El-Erian added: "For the UK, all this translates into another hit to the cost of living and less flexibility for both fiscal and monetary policy responses."

View 5 Images Woman walks past pro-government political mural in Tehran (Image: Getty Images)

The UN Trade & Development warned the continues military escalation in the waterway and disrupted shipping flows have led to "ripple effects go far beyond the region, affecting energy markets, maritime transport and global supply chains".

Article continues below

It said: "Higher energy, fertilizer and transport costs – including freight rates, bunker fuel prices and insurance premiums – may increase food costs and intensify cost-of-living pressures, particularly for the most vulnerable."

Despite this, shipping expert Lars Jensen told the BBC Trump's new blockade "will halt a very tiny trickle of vessels". The expert said: "In the greater scheme of things, it doesn't really change anything." Jensen added: "First of all, there's very few ships that pass. There's even fewer of those that pay, and those that pay will already be subject to American sanctions."

News.title: Man falls from Jet2 plane at Manchester Airport as air accident investigators sent
News.content:
Man falls from Jet2 plane at Manchester Airport as air accident investigators sent

A man, believed to be an aircraft engineer, was seriously injured after falling from the back of a Jet2 plane at Manchester Airport. Paramedics were scrambled to the scene at around 8am

View 2 Images (Image: UGC)

Investigators have been called in after a man plummeted from a plane at a UK airport over the weekend.

‌



Air accident investigators were dispatched to the scene after a man tragically fell from a plane at Manchester Airport on Saturday (April 11).

‌



The individual, thought to be an aircraft engineer, was left with severe injuries including fractures to his arm and leg after plummeting from the rear of the aircraft. Paramedics rushed to the airport around 8am following the incident.

‌



Photos taken at the scene depict ambulances and fire service response vehicles surrounding a Jet2 plane. The airline later confirmed that a 'full' investigation had been initiated. It is believed the man was a contractor working for Jet2 at the time.

In a subsequent update, the Air Accident Investigations Branch (AAIB) confirmed that specialist investigators were sent to the scene and investigations commenced, reports the Manchester Evening News.

‌



A statement recently issued by the AAIB read: "On Saturday 11 April the AAIB were informed of an accident involving a person falling from an aircraft at Manchester Airport. The AAIB dispatched a team to Manchester Airport on Saturday to begin an investigation into the accident."

View 2 Images (Image: UGC)

In images from the scene, the aircraft can be seen with a door open near the tail. Mobile stairs used for passengers are also visible nearby.

Article continues below

Manchester Airport confirmed North West Ambulance Service attended the incident. It's understood the plane was scheduled to depart to Tenerife.

A spokesperson for Jet2 stated: "We are aware of an incident that took place at Manchester Airport this morning (Saturday 11th April) involving an individual from a third-party provider.

"We are unable to confirm further details at present, however, can confirm that a full investigation has been launched. We are doing our best to provide support to everyone who needs it."

News.title: Coachella drama as festival-goer caught in freak accident leaving head bleeding
News.content:
Coachella drama as festival-goer caught in freak accident leaving head bleeding

A Coachella festival goer was left with a gash on their head following an incident during DJ John Summit's set at the iconic music event

View 3 Images John Summit performs at the Do LaB (Image: Getty Images for Coachella)

A Coachella festival attendee was involved in an ordeal that left them with a gash to the head. The festival goer was injured after a heavy light fixture fell onto her.

‌



The incident took place after DJ and producer John Summit took the Do LaB stage for a surprise set on Friday. The moment left one audience member with a bloodied face as the light plummeted into the crowd halfway through the show.

‌



An eyewitness said the unfortunate attendee was left in a mess from the incident as it "gashed her head open". Joey Freshour, who had been in the crowd at the time said on Instagram: "Thirty minutes in, we were all dancing [and] having a good time.

‌



Adele makes rare public appearance with son at Justin Bieber's Coachella performance READ MORE :

Katy Perry makes thinly veiled dig about Justin Bieber's Coachella set as fans divided READ MORE :

View 3 Images The incident happened during John Summit's DJ set (Image: Getty Images for Coachella)

"I'm chit-chatting, having a good time, talking to one of my friends. I look over, out of the glimpse of my eye - probably four people in front of me - and see the light structure. It had fallen and hit a girl directly on the side of the head, cutting her head open directly on the side, right here."

After pointing to his temple, he continued: "Leading her to be bleeding out the side of her head... You can see little red dots on the side of the light in the video and basically that's her blood. Not good."

‌



He also spoke further about the incident in an interview with SFGate. He explained that audience members nearby had tried to signal for medical help. Three men picked the woman up and took her to the medical tent to get the help she needed.

His video of the scene showed the large light fixture lying on the ground. He then panned the camera upward to show the cables in place to hold it aloft.

He explained that the DJ hadn't been aware of the incident and claimed it was caused by strong winds. The elements were also said to have caused Justin Bieber to take to the stage late the following night.

‌



View 3 Images A light fell during John Summit's set (Image: Getty Images for Coachella)

But the wind was the least of Justin's worries, with some fans slamming his "lazy" efforts. Many expected Justin, 32, to be full of energy on his return to the stage. But he left them confused with his display.

Instead of the high-octane performance they had anticipated, Justin sat on a stool in front of the packed crowd. He was seen scrolling through YouTube videos of his songs on a laptop while streaming his earlier music as part of a brief 12-song medley.

Article continues below

"Not Justin Bieber scammed Coachella out of $10 million to play songs off of YouTube…” fumed one user on X, formerly known as Twitter. Another slammed the star's set as "the laziest performances of all time".

However, some fans were left to fight his corner, saying it was actually a good set. Another user claimed the signer was a "mastermind". They claimed people "won't understand" what he was doing as he improvised on stage.

News.title: Southport inquiry to provide answers after authorities failed to stop killer
News.content:
Southport inquiry to provide answers after authorities failed to stop killer

Bebe King, six, Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, were killed at a Taylor Swift-themed dance event in July 2024

View 6 Images Phase one of the report will be released at midday (Image: PA)

The inquiry into the horrific Southport murders which promised to “provide answers for the victims and their families” is expected to be highly critical of public services that ignored the threat posed by the murderer.

‌



Described as “one of the most egregious crimes in our country’s history”, Bebe King, six, Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, were killed at a Taylor Swift-themed dance event in July 2024.

‌



Monster Axel Rudakubana, now 19, was sentenced to a minimum of 52 years in prison after pleading guilty to the murders in January last year. He also admitted 10 counts of attempted murder, producing ricin, and possessing an Al Qaeda training manual.

‌



After the killings it emerged he had been referred to the government’s Prevent programme - which aims to stop people becoming radicalised - three times.

6 View 6 Images Bebe King (Image: PA) 6 View 6 Images Alice da Silva Aguiar (Image: PA)

‌



View 6 Images Elsie Dot Stancombe (Image: PA)

Inquiry chairman Sir Adrian Fulford will release phase one of his report into the stabbings at midday. It looks into the policing, the criminal justice system and the agencies involved with the killer’s care, education and mental health. Phase two will look into the wider issue of young people being drawn into extremism.

At least six public bodies are expected to be criticised in Sir Adrian's findings, reports the Daily Mail.

‌



When he opened the inquiry Sir Adrian said: “None of the most powerful adjectives even begin to suffice. There are no words that adequately describe what occurred and I am not going to try, and then fail, to find them."

He asked the media not to use the police-issued mugshot of the killer taken after his arrest, which victims and their families said was a “terrifying and singularly distressing image”. The families have repeated this request this week.

Sir Adrian added: “This inquiry is expected to act as a real engine for change given the unparalleled nature of what occurred. I am determined it will not turn into an exercise of papering over the cracks."

‌



He vowed to make recommendations that would stop others “who may be drawn to treating their fellow human beings in such a cruel and inhuman way,” adding: “Although no solution will be foolproof, we can identify all of the robust steps which should be taken to protect ourselves, and particularly the most vulnerable, from horrors of this kind.

“And this must be undertaken at speed, to provide answers for the victims and their families and to identify all of the changes that urgently need to be made.”

Talking about the Prevent counter-terror programme, he said: “The state’s well established counter measures against ‘terrorism’ are vital. But does that machinery adequately address young people who are drawn into extreme violence without an accompanying commitment to a particular religious or political cause?

‌



View 6 Images Chair Sir Adrian Fulford will publish his report tomorrow (Image: PA)

“Put shortly, should there be more effective mechanisms for identifying those who are contemplating serious offences, for monitoring their behaviour and for controlling their activities?"

The inquiry also heard harrowing evidence from the parents of the three girls, who fought back tears as they recalled their loss.

‌



Jenni Stancombe, 35, said: “Elsie only went to dance and make bracelets but we never got to bring her home. I walk past an empty bed every night, I stare into her room praying this nightmare will end, but it never does. We live it every day."

View 6 Images (L-R), Chris Long and Jenni Stancombe, Uncle and Mother of Elsie Dot Stancombe; Lauren King and Ben King, parents of Bebe King and Alexandra Aguiar and Sergio Aguiar, parents of Alice Aguiar (Image: Getty Images)

Alice's parents found their daughter on the ground surrounded by medics. Alexandra, 34, and Sergio Aguiar, 38, faced a 13-hour wait in Southport hospital before doctors told them their only child was dead.

Article continues below

A statement read by their solicitor said: “I have never experienced fear like it, not knowing where my little girl was. I ran around looking into little injured girls' faces searching for my baby girl. After what seemed like hours I found Alice. She was lying on the floor with people around her tending to her wounds. My happy, loving, innocent little girl - hurt by a monster.”

Bebe's mum Lauren, 42, fell to her knees screaming after she was told on a street corner that her daughter was dead. “The impact of losing her can barely be described. On that day, being told over the phone by my husband that a man had gone into the dance class with a knife and that they couldn't find Bebe? The hours walking around in the intense heat not knowing whether she was alive or not? praying to God that she was. Then being told in public, on a street corner, that my child was dead.

“I replay that day over and over, every single day. I picture him attacking my beautiful Bebe, imagine her fear, her pain. His eyes - his evil eyes - never leave my mind.”

News.title: Man 'drank beer and watched after starting New York building fire' killing four
News.content:
Man 'drank beer and watched after starting New York building fire' killing four

Roman Almatitla, 38, has been accused of starting a fire at a three-storey building in Flushing, New York, which left four people dead including a three-year-old girl

View 2 Images Firefighters tackling the blaze in Flushing (Image: WABC-TV)

A man is alleged to have drunk a beer and watched after setting fire to a New York building which left four people dead.

‌



Roman Almatitla, 38, has been charged with arson, murder, and assault all in connection to the fire that took place at a three-storey building in Flushing last month.

‌



Three adults and a three-year-old girl died in the tragedy where others had to jump out of windows to escape the blaze, according to Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz.

‌



View 2 Images Four people died in the tragedy (Image: WABC-TV)

UK to sizzle at 22C within days as heatwave hits 6 counties READ MORE :

Keir Starmer sends warning to US and Iran after peace talks break down READ MORE :

Chengri Cui, 49, Shin Chie Ming, 61, and the young girl, were found dead at the scene from smoke inhalation. Hong Zhao, 64, leapt from a window and sustained brain trauma and numerous broken bones, before later being pronounced dead at the hospital.

Several other people were injured, including two firefighters who had to be rescued from the building after a staircase collapsed.

‌



Almatitla admitted he had no particular reason to attend the building that day, reportedly said prosecutors, and he is alleged to have started the fire out of anger at losing his job that day.

He entered the building a number of times before heading to a petrol station across the street where he bought a beer, stole another and asked the cashier behind the register to borrow a lighter, said the District Attorney.

CCTV footage showed him at the petrol station and then he returned to the building where he followed a woman inside as she opened the door to go in.

‌



It is then that he allegedly lit a piece of paper with matches before dropping into a trash can near the exit for the second and third floors.

While the first floor of the building is occupied by a commercial space, the second and third are all residential apartments. A witness, speaking to WNBC, said they saw two people jump from the second floor, with one woman shouting: “My baby, my baby.”

Since 2020, the property has been issued with more than 50 violations by the Department of Buildings. Inspectors also found an illegal gambling business operating on the first floor in 2023, during which a $23,000 fine was issued to the organizers.

Article continues below

The latest violation, a failure to maintain, came in January this year after investigators unearthed extension cables running from the first to third floors.

News.title: British expat moved to UAE for dream life but claims he was tortured by police
News.content:
British expat moved to UAE for dream life but claims he was tortured by police

A British millionaire who used to dine with Dubai's elite spent four years locked up in the expat hotspot - now he has issued a warning to people looking to move to the UAE

View 6 Images Millionaire Albert Douglas spent four years in jail in the United Arab Emirates (Image: albertdouglas.com)

A British expat who became a successful businessman in the UAE has warned people considering going to the desert country to "be careful" after he was locked up for years.

‌



Albert Douglas, 63, said he still suffers from the scars of being imprisoned in Dubai's notorious jails. The Brit moved to Dubai in the 1990s and made the most of the property boom and transformation of the desert land - becoming rich and successful in the process.

‌



At one point he drove around in a Rolls Royce and attended glamorous events and dinners with Dubai's elite - including ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum who reportedly gifted Albert a pet tiger cub - but this luxury life all came crashing down.

‌



View 6 Images Albert Douglas with his son Wolfgang

Albert moved to Dubai permanently with his wife Naomi, in 2002, and set up a flooring business, named Alomi Real Wood Floors, which supplied to buildings including the Burj Khalifa and the City Walk. The Brit at one point even lived in a £6million mansion of the famous Palm Jumeirah island.

Albert worked with his son Wolfgang, who set up his own company named TimberWolf Flooring, but the son soon fell into issues recouping money for multi-million-pound government projects he was working on, according to the Daily Mail.

‌



View 6 Images Albert having surgery in the UAE after being 'attacked by guards'

Wolfgang flew back to the UK for a medical procedure, in 2019, and Albert also flew back to the UK but decided to head back to Dubai to carry on work. Albert was arrested at Dubai international airport and fined £2.5million and sentenced to three years behind bars, after UAE authorities were not able to reach his son.

The dad claimed he had no links to his son's business at the time of his arrest, expect being listed on a legal document for the company that was started in 2007. Albert also said authorities in the UAE said a cheque the 63-year-old signed had bounced but he had strongly denied these claims.

‌



View 6 Images Albert sent a warning to Brits looking to move to the UAE

Albert was released on bail, after taking his case to the supreme court but failing, then attempted to escape the UAE by crossing the border into Oman, in February 2021. The dad was caught and arrested by soldiers.

Albert claimed he was attacked and his family alleged that this led him to develop Alzheimer's disease and suffer with several strokes. He was kept in several jails and claimed he was tortured while being help in captivity. The dad alleged that he was deprived of water, food and medical treatment.

‌



View 6 Images Albert at his daughter Abigail's wedding in 2009

He also claimed that he saw fellow inmates being raped and dying by suicide. Albert also claimed he weighed by 9st 6lbs when he was eventually released from jail, despite being 12st 8lbs when he went in. Albert revealed the pain he still suffers with to this day and said: "God didn't give me these injuries. I suffer now from blackouts. I had my broken shoulder, which wasn't properly fixed. I had three fingers that were broken. I have a back injury."

The dad was handed a two year sentence in February 2021 before it was reduced to 18 months. Despite this, he stayed in prison much longer and was released in May 2025 after the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention had looked into his case.

Article continues below

View 6 Images Wolfgang (left) Albert (right) (Image: Jam Press/Detained In Dubai)

Albert sent a warning to other Brits looking to move their lives to the UAE, according to the Daily Mail, and said: "Be careful and be aware of what happened to me - it could very, very easily happen to you." He added: "I assure you, I'm not the only one. There are dozens, even hundreds of people that are in the same situation. It's endemic in their system: not a one-off, it's accepted."

Albert also warned: "In the UAE, there are basically no human rights. Speaking your mind in any way detrimental to the government of the UAE can get you put in jail, and when you are in jail, you are under scrutiny all the time."

One of the House’s most conservative members finds himself in an uncomfortable spot as he defends his push for the U.S. to expand its cap on temporary foreign workers while facing criticism from members of his own party for supposedly betraying Donald Trump’s agenda.

Rep. Andy Harris is Maryland’s lone Republican congressman and chair of the far-right House Freedom Caucus, a collection of lawmakers typically aligned closely with the president but often in conflict with House leadership over funding levels and other issues.

Harris was profiled by Politico this week as he pushes for the U.S. to expand the cap on H-2B visas, which allow a maximum of 66,000 workers to come into the United States every year and perform non-agricultural work around the country. In Harris’s home state and district, Maryland’s Eastern Shore, the immigrant workers are an important source of labor for Maryland’s often-struggling seafood industry.

Trump’s first and second terms have seen White House and Department of Homeland Security officials aim to issue a lower number of H-2B visas than the law permits. But Harris, Politico reports, visited the West Wing at a crucial moment this January and persuaded the administration to hike 2026’s count to just under the legal cap; 65,000 visas will be issued this year by DHS.

“This is not an immigration issue — this is a temporary foreign worker issue,” he insisted to Politico.

open image in gallery Rep. Andy Harris of Maryland is defending his call to expand H-2B visas from the anti-immigrant right ( POOL/AFP via Getty Images )

Harris is one of a group of Republicans working with the Senate on the DIGNIDAD Act, a broad piece of immigration legislation that would represent the most serious effort by Congress to address the issue in years. It would expand E-verification tools and requirements while also providing a path for currently undocumented workers to live and work freely in America, though stopping short of making full citizenship possible.

For companies that rely in whole or part on workers using H-2B visas, the legislation is massively important because it revives a provision once championed by another Maryland lawmaker, Sen. Barbara Mikulski. Mikulski, a Democrat and legend of the upper chamber who died in 2017, led the effort for Congress to exclude returning foreign workers from the yearly caps, an effective gradual expansion of those caps, which was then brought to an end in the first year of Donald Trump’s first term. Harris is a key ally of that policy, demonstrating its bipartisan appeal.

But that isn’t an explanation that is gaining any traction with the anti-immigration hardliners in the Republican Party, including War Room podcast host Steve Bannon, who raged about the expansion of the DHS’s H-2B visas with the head of the far-right Immigration Accountability Project during a recent episode.

“Where’s your compassion for Americans?” the head of that organization, Rosemary Jenks, questioned the lawmakers working on the DIGNIDAD Act during the interview.

“There are 20 Republicans...who are basically passing off this ‘Dignity Act’, which should be called the ’SAAW Act’, for ‘Screw All American Workers’, that’s what it should be called because that’s what it does,” she added, claiming that “tens of millions” of immigrants would receive “mass amnesty” for them and their families.

Other members of the Trump administration, like Stephen Miller, remain opposed to the expansion of H-2B visas and have accused lawmakers who support it of importing “monsters” and “mass murderers”, echoing the worst of his boss’s anti-immigrant rhetoric against various ethnic communities.

“The Democrat Party mass imported monsters who are mass murdering Americans. And the Democrat Party and its corrupt judges are fighting relentlessly to keep them here,” Miller wrote on X last week.

It isn’t just anti-immigration groups like Jenks’s that oppose the increase in H-2B visas. Some unions have spoken out against the announcement as well, claiming it will drive down wages for all workers.

open image in gallery Maryland's Eastern Shore is known for its crabbing industry, which relies on H-2B visa workers every year ( AFP via Getty Images )

“Flooding the labor market with exploitable foreign workers drives down wages and weakens the standard for all workers, the Laborers' International Union of North America (LIUNA) said in a statement. “If employers truly face hiring challenges, the answer is better wages, safer conditions, and real workforce investment.”

Harris enters the spring having cheated his political death. The Maryland state Senate, controlled by Democrats, is refusing to bring up redistricting legislation championed by Gov. Wes Moore that was aimed at redrawing his seat and making it more favorable to a Democratic candidate and possibly allowing Democrats to take the last of the state’s eight congressional seats. They already control the other seven. Moore’s bid was launched in response to an effort to do the same in Texas and other red states by Republicans, including Donald Trump.

The congressman won his eighth term in the House by more than 20 points over his Democratic challenger in 2024. In that same cycle, he won his primary by 60 points. He’s likely insulated from any challenge on the right, unless he were to somehow lose the support and endorsement of the president.

Trump did just that to several other Republicans this cycle. In Texas, he withheld his endorsement for incumbent Sen. John Cornyn, who subsequently came in less than two percentage points ahead of his closest rival, Ken Paxton, in the first round of the primary election for his seat in March.

Another sitting Republican senator, Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, is now facing a primary challenger backed by the president, though Cassidy’s support has not appeared to crater just yet.

The government is expected to close down 11 more so-called “asylum hotels” next week as it tries to move faster on tackling illegal immigration.

The closure of the controversial hotels is part of the government’s plan to end hotel accommodation for irregular migrants altogether and linked to a meeting this week on the new contract for asylum accommodation.

The hotels have become a magnet for rightwing anti-migrant protesters and centred around claims of attacks by asylum seekers on women and girls.

Notably, the Bell in Epping became a focus of far right demonstrations with the local Tory-led council unsuccessfully blocking its use as a holding place for asylum seekers waiting for their applications to be administered.

Police presence outside the Bell Hotel in Epping, Essex (Lucy North/PA) ( PA Archive )

Latest government statistics show there are around 200 hotels in use, accommodating about 30,000 asylum seekers. More than 70,000 other asylum seekers live in other types of accommodation such as shared housing or military barracks.

According to The Guardian, the Home Office is due to hold a private event this week, described as an “industry day” for potential future providers of asylum accommodation.

The department has not disclosed details of the time and venue and it is reported that those attending have to sign a non disclosure agreement (NDA).

The meeting is understood to relate to the re-tendering of asylum contracts from 1 September 2029 until 31 August 2036, with a possible option to extend to 31 August 2039. The new contract, known as Future Asylum Contracts Accommodation, has been valued at approximately £10bn and will enact the government aim of moving away from reliance on hotel accommodation.

Controversially, the Home Office uses part of the already reduced overseas aid budget to fund asylum accommodation in a practice known as “in donor refugee costs”.

These costs amounted to around £2.8bn in 2024 to £2.4bn in 2025.

The Home Office has been asked to comment on the claims but not responded.

A Home Office spokesperson told The Guardian: “This government is removing the incentives drawing illegal migrants to Britain and ramping up removals of those with no right to be here. That is why we are closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into basic accommodation including ex-military sites.

“The population in asylum hotels has fallen by nearly 20 per cent in the last year and by 45 per cent since the peak under the previous government, cutting costs by nearly £1bn.”

News.title: The Masters LIVE: Justin Rose and Rory McIlroy battle for lead in thrilling final round
News.content:
Rory McIlroy looks for answers as Masters lead vanishes

The Masters is set for a thrilling finale as Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose battle for the lead again at Augusta National.

McIlroy had begun the day as co-leader having seen a six-shot advantage slip away on Saturday as Cameron Young surged, but has steadied after a wobble to remain right in the mix. The Northern Irishman is seeking to become only the fourth back-to-back winner of the green jacket having pipped Rose in a dramatic play-off last year to complete a career grand slam.

Young remains right in contention alongside compatriot Russell Henley, with Scottie Scheffler lurking ominously, too. Tyrrell Hatton, meanwhile, has set the clubhouse lead at -10 after a sublime 66, putting the pressure on the later starters as they head down the second nine with plenty of twists and turns still in store.

A Nebraska man accused of killing a hog farmer and kidnapping his estranged wife was subsequently pronounced dead at a nearby hospital, according to authorities.

Wesley Absher, 40, was initially arrested following the shooting on Tuesday, in which he killed 44-year-old Brian Gabel at the farm the victim owned.

After carrying out the attack, Absher kidnapped his own ex-wife, who had been at the farm at the time, before driving her three miles away and allegedly assaulting her.

He is then believed to have shot himself, Nebraska State Police said.

Absher’s wife was able to drive to the Polk County Sheriff’s Office in Osceola and report both the shooting and assault just after 1:30 a.m. Tuesday.

open image in gallery Wesley Absher, a Nebraska man accused of killing a hog farmer and kidnapping his estranged wife, has died in hospital, according to state police ( Platte County Sheriff's Office )

Deputies secured both scenes and Absher was taken to Bryan Health West Campus in Lincoln with life-threatening injuries, where he later died from his injuries.

NSP confirmed that Absher, who had bonded out of jail just days before the shooting occurred, was in the process of divorcing his wife when the incident occurred.

The woman was taken to Columbus Community Hospital for treatment for her injuries, which were non-life-threatening.

According to court documents, Absher had previously been found guilty of second-degree assault and terroristic threats in a separate case that involved the same woman on February 8.

open image in gallery Absher was arrested following the incident Tuesday, in which he arrived at the farm, owned by 44-year-old Brian Gabel, and allegedly shot him ( Dubas Funeral Home )

In that incident, Absher was accused of threatening his wife and assaulting her with a weapon. He also threatened to kill himself, the documents showed.

He was arrested at the hospital and on April 1 he accepted a plea deal. He was released on bond on April 3 and was due to be sentenced on June 10.

The Independent has contacted the Polk County Sheriff’s Office and Nebraska State Police for comment.

Gabel’s funeral was held on Friday.

A stampede at a mountaintop fortress popular with tourists in northern Haiti has killed at least 25 people and injured dozens of others, authorities said, revising an earlier, higher number of fatalities.

Municipal authorities in the city of Cap-Haïtien in a statement said that Saturday's stampede in Milot "resulted in numerous cases of asphyxiation, trampling and loss of consciousness." Authorities said dozens of people who attended traditional festivities at the historical site were taken to hospitals while many others were reported missing.

“According to preliminary information ... a situation of severe overcrowding, linked in particular to deficiencies in crowd management measures, triggered a stampede,” local authorities said in the statement.

The Haitian National Police in a separate statement said it had opened an investigation to determine the exact cause of incident. The investigation led authorities to update the death toll to 25 fatalities. Autopsies were underway on Sunday.

Police said 30 people remained hospitalized. The agency also asked the population to continue to cooperate with authorities and avoid spreading rumors.

Haiti’s government offered its condolences to the families of the victims of the incident at the Citadelle Laferrière.

Some of the victims’ bodies remained at the site on Sunday.

Donaldson Jean said his sister had traveled there after studying diligently to get the grades necessary to be part of a school field trip for the best students. He sobbed after carrying her body, which had been covered with a white tarp.

“Morning and night, she was studying for the genius program,” he said. “She would come and ask me to help with homework before dinner. Look how (I) lost her”
